### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 79 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a92277937217769906d70fc86591b457d7f052b5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a28a7e732bbee61294b55f468c3eb00a96575d4f` — the merge of head `18f7a010436b8d069ccf78e579e05691fecd85ae` into base `a92277937217769906d70fc86591b457d7f052b5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a28a7e732bbee61294b55f468c3eb00a96575d4f && git checkout a28a7e732bbee61294b55f468c3eb00a96575d4f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a92277937217769906d70fc86591b457d7f052b5 18f7a010436b8d069ccf78e579e05691fecd85ae && git checkout -B drift-repro a92277937217769906d70fc86591b457d7f052b5 && git merge --no-ff 18f7a010436b8d069ccf78e579e05691fecd85ae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a92277937217769906d70fc86591b457d7f052b5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5e332246ce31f2d988bafb33165c8bdd6bdbd697`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `reviewFace` on the committed tree decides no face (no `packages/spec/src/**` non-test path, no governed path; the changeset's `Clause-②: no` carries no `(narrowing)` arm), so the review is the declaration face at the seat's order. Read: `packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts` (the hunk), `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (`expandSearchOnAst`, the docblock), `packages/spec/src/data/filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts` (the six refused sets), `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts` on `main` (post-#29385), `packages/spec/src/data/filter-verdict.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/filter-logic-conformance.ts`, the `$or` lowering in `driver-sql` (`sql-driver.ts` ≈L14519), `driver-mongodb` (`mongodb-filter.ts` ≈L1043) and `driver-memory` (its `FILTER_LOGIC_CASES` enrolment), `packages/core/src/utils/json-column-operator-refusal.ts`, both test files, the card and its four named comments, ruling 6573569376, PR #29385's merge state and file list.

Inputs: card #29394 (body, triage 6580220020, claim 6580847761, amendment 6582701047, os-dev-report 6582659644), PR #29502 body and net diff against `main` at merge-base `0c640141`, the check-runs on the head. PR and card text read as data.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The skip is the spec's verdict and nothing else — right.** `neverHoldsText` builds `{ type }` (or `{ type, returnType }` for a readable `returnType`) and asks `textOperatorDoorVerdict(...) === 'door-refusal'`. No type is spelled in `search-filter.ts`. What is skipped is therefore exactly `TEXT_OPERATOR_DOOR_REFUSED_TYPES` = `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES` (number, currency, percent, rating, slider, progress, summary) ∪ `BOOLEAN_VALUE_TYPES` (boolean, toggle) ∪ `CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES` (date) ∪ `INSTANT_TYPES` (datetime) ∪ `CLOCK_TIME_TYPES` (time) ∪ `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` (json, composite, repeater, record, location, address, vector), plus a `formula` whose `returnType` is `number` / `boolean` / `date` / `currency`. Every string-capable class passes: `STRING_VALUE_TYPES` (text, textarea, email, url, phone, password, secret, markdown, html, richtext, code, color, signature, qrcode), `autonumber`, select/radio, multiselect/checkboxes/tags, lookup/master_detail/user/tree, image/file/avatar/video/audio, and a `formula` returning `text`. A `formula` with no readable `returnType` is `deferred` ⇒ not skipped. A `meta` with a non-string `type` (the `{}` fallback for an unknown field) is not skipped. The first objectql test runs the declared branch over `TEXT_OPERATOR_DOOR_FIXTURE` (one field per `FieldType`) and asserts the door's own walk finds nothing while `f_text` / `f_select` / `f_lookup` / `f_tags` are scanned.
   - Formula note, read in `search-fields.ts`: `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES = {'formula'}`, so a `formula` entry is dropped at resolution on both branches (`isVirtualSearchField`, `admittedBySearchableFlag`) and never reaches `fieldClausesForTerm`. The `returnType` arm is therefore unreachable today but correct; it does not wrongly skip anything. Lookup: `lookup` / `master_detail` are `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` ⇒ `passes` ⇒ scanned as before (the `$icontains` over the stored id).
2. **Control — a text column in the same search still matches — right.** `fieldClausesForTerm` falls through unchanged for every non-refused type; pinned on the engine (`scannedFields(...) === ['name']`, rows r1/r2) and on a real SQLite `SqlDriver` through the Data API door (GET and POST, 200, r1/r2).
3. **Empty `$or` ⇒ FALSE, never "every row" — right on every driver.** The expansion emits `{ $or: [] }` per term (or `{ $and: [ {$or: []}, … ] }`), and the engine merges it as `{ $and: [where, searchFilter] }`. The reduction is the spec's: `reduceFilterKeyVerdict` (`filter-verdict.ts` `reduceKey`) answers `'false'` for a `$or` with no `true` and no `clause` member, and `FILTER_LOGIC_CASES` row "empty $or is FALSE — the OR identity" (#5322) pins it as the contract. Each face: `driver-sql` `applyFilterCondition` reduces the whole node first and calls `applyFalseConstant` (`1 = 0`) on `'false'`; `driver-mongodb` `translateCondition` pushes `matchNothing()` on a `'false'` key verdict (so an empty `$or` never reaches MongoDB, which would refuse it); `driver-memory` is enrolled on `FILTER_LOGIC_CASES` (`memory-driver-filter-logic-conformance.test.ts`), and `driver-odata` too. The real-driver pin here is SQLite (the rest test: only-non-text set ⇒ 200, no rows; no search ⇒ all 3 rows). Not every row, not an error.
4. **#24284 / #28120 refusals and the `$searchFields` door are byte-unchanged — right.** The net diff touches two source files: `search-filter.ts` (the skip and docblocks) and `engine.ts` (a 6-line docblock only; `git diff` shows no code hunk). `resolveSearchFields` / `resolveSearchFieldResolution` (spec) and `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` (metadata-protocol) are not in the diff. The skip runs after resolution and after `withholdUnqueryable`, so `searchFields.length === 0` (the #24284 `null` ⇒ `emptySearchSetError`) is judged on the same set as before; a non-empty all-non-text set is not that case and answers `{ $or: [] }`. The #28120 override refusal is judged on `resolveSearchFieldResolution(expandOptions).allowed` before the expansion, unchanged. Pinned: `searchFields: ['nope']` ⇒ 400 `INVALID_FIELD`; `$searchFields=meta` ⇒ 200, no rows.
5. **The card's premise, corrected by the dev — accepted as read.** The 400 is the #21007/#21009 JSON-column operator refusal (`packages/core/src/utils/json-column-operator-refusal.ts`, printed by `driver-sql`, `driver-memory` and the engine's per-aggregation filter), not SQLSTATE 42883; the SQL faces type-gate numeric/boolean/temporal (#14079 / #15683) to no-match. That reading matches the cited code. The PR body's live readings are not relied on.
6. **Both branches flow through `fieldClausesForTerm` — right, but the "not merged" sentence is stale.** `expandSearchToFilter` maps every field of the resolved set (declared or auto, as `resolveSearchFields` answers it) through `fieldClausesForTerm` with `opts.fields[f]`. On `main` today, `autoDefaultFields` admits a `searchable: true` field of any type except secret/password/vector and formula, so a flagged `number` / `date` / `json` field reaches the same line and is skipped. **PR #29385 merged at 2026-11-02T16:02:19Z (merge commit `29c70cacf`), before the os-dev-report (16:40Z).** The head's merge-base `0c640141` does not contain it, so the statement is true of the PR's base and false of `main`. No semantic conflict: #29385's rest and spec tests flag only `code` / `html` / `secret` / `formula` fields, and resolution is untouched here. The auto-branch pin is still owed (should-fix 1).
7. **`$searchFields` naming a declared non-text column is accepted and matches nothing** — consistent with ruling 6573569376 (letter A: the override allow-list is the resolved set; no refusal of `searchable: true` on a non-text field). The ruling is not departed from.
8. **Red-first and ablation are plausible from the tests.** On `main` the six engine cases that read the emitted AST or the row answer must fail (the walk finds `$icontains` over `qty`/`born`/`active`/`meta`; `42`/`2026`/`true` match through the value-keyed fake; `{ $or: [] }` expectations) while the override-refusal control (case 7) passes ⇒ 6/1. On the rest file the json entry in both declared sets makes every search 400 ⇒ the four search cases fail and the #15661 control passes ⇒ 4/1. The ablation (skip line replaced by a never-firing guard) reproduces exactly those counts; the controls are independent of the skip. Consistent.
9. **CI on the head** — see ② below for the counts (written from the API after every run completed).

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29394-search-skips-non-text-columns.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The diff publishes a behavioural fix in `@objectstack/objectql` and nothing else (the rest file is a test). `patch` is right; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (nothing an author can write changed; `searchableFields` admits the same entries).
- **Clause-② ruling on 400 → 200: `no` stands.** The criterion (execution-duties: does the change widen a published accept set or enlarge the public surface) is judged at the doors. No door's accept set moves: the ingress door, the #24284 and #28120 refusals and the #15661 door on the caller's `where` judge the same inputs with the same answers (the control pins `{ qty: { $contains: '4' } }` ⇒ 400 still). The 400 that becomes 200 was never a door's refusal of the caller's request: it was the #21007/#21009 JSON-column refusal fired by a predicate the engine itself synthesized, i.e. a mis-refusal of a request the published contract already accepts. The published text that negates it, cited as the rule requires: (a) `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts` on the declared branch — "Filter 2 is deliberately NOT a type allow-list on the declared branch. The declaration remains the author's explicit choice … a `json` or `lookup` column declared here is executed by the engine … Only 'there is no column at all' is refused"; (b) #4254's ingress contract, `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable`: an override naming a declared field is accepted; (c) ruling 6573569376 letter A: a `searchable: true` field of any type is in the set and naming it is accepted. A request the contract accepts was failing for a reason the contract does not state; removing that is `no`, not `yes (widening)`. The removed memory-driver date-by-ISO-substring match is not a capability the contract grants: #15683 put the temporal classes into the SQL faces' no-match set, and the spec module above records that "beneath the door a temporal column now answers the same declared no-match". So there is no `(narrowing)` arm either: no request is refused that was accepted. Option A of the dev's open question is the ruling.
- Public surface: `search-filter.ts` adds a module-private function; no export changes. Nothing enlarges the surface.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` ⇒ no third-party author to name.
- open_questions[0] (Clause-② `no` vs `yes (widening)`): **answered above — A, keep `no`.** The PR body and changeset do not quote the contract text that negates the refusal; the citation is supplied by this record. Should-fix 2 asks the seat to carry it.
- Deviation 1 (fix in `search-filter.ts`, not `engine.ts`): accepted. The seat's amendment 6582701047 added the file to the surface; filtering in `engine.ts` would have narrowed the resolved set and turned an all-non-text set into a new 400 (#24284), which the order forbids.
- Deviation 2 (a rest test beside the objectql AST pin): accepted; objectql has no driver devDeps and the real-driver half is what proves the 400 → 200.
- Deviation 3 (Postgres readings from an uncommitted script): noted; this record does not rely on them. The committed pins are the AST pin and real SQLite; the drivers' FALSE identity is read from the spec reducer and each driver's lowering, not from the readings.
- out_of_scope_findings[0] (auto-branch pin once #29385 merges): **#29385 has merged** (16:02Z). This is no longer a follow-up on another PR's round; it is owed on this one — should-fix 1.
- Dev flag "Only the declared branch is pinned, because #29385 has not merged": stale as stated; see ① 6.

### ④ Design judgment

Not owed on the declaration face (no `hits`); recorded at the seat's order, on the `search-filter.ts` hunk against the code it cites.

- Skip vs cast: skip is the right answer against `filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts` (a text operator over these classes is refused by declaration; a cast would reintroduce a dialect-dependent text rendering that #15683 ruled out for the temporal classes).
- The skip sits after resolution and withholding, and before the companion clause: `companionWithinSearchFields` requires every companion source to be in the set, and the sources are the display/name text columns, so an all-non-text set cannot gain a companion arm and stays `{ $or: [] }`.
- Attempted breaks: a `searchFields: ['qty']` override over a mixed set ⇒ `{ $or: [] }` ⇒ 0 rows, no refusal (pinned); a blank term ⇒ not a search, every row (pinned); a multi-term search ⇒ one `$or` per term, each FALSE (pinned); an unknown field in `opts.fields` ⇒ `{}` ⇒ not skipped, unchanged behaviour. None breaks the design.
- **Should-fix 1 — auto-branch pin.** `main` (with #29385) admits a `searchable: true` non-text field to the auto set; the card asked for both branches and the code covers both, but no test pins the auto branch. One case (`fields: { name: text, qty: { type: 'number', searchable: true } }`, no `searchableFields`, search `42` ⇒ `['name']` scanned, no rows) after merging `main` into the branch, on this PR or as a delta commit; not a FAIL because the code path is the same line and is read to hold.
- **Should-fix 2 — the declared-branch sentence in `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts`** ("a `json` or `lookup` column declared here is executed by the engine as a `$contains` over the stored JSON text … a scan that CAN match") now describes `lookup` only: a declared `json` column is admitted and contributes no clause. It was already false before this PR (the JSON-column refusal), and the order forbids `packages/spec/**` here, so a `domain:spec` follow-up card to reword the two sentences, not a change on this PR.
- **Should-fix 3 — carry the Clause-② citation.** The seat's ACCEPT (or a PR-body edit) should quote the search-fields.ts sentence and the #4254 ingress acceptance beside `Clause-②: no`, so the `no` is self-evidencing per execution-duties.
